clue.text: Bound to provide grassland parking

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassland
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A rule obliging someone to make pasture available for car parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'obliged' (bound to provide), but it is the definition in its jumping sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a jump, so the two words are synonyms as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Note set-up for a public school

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word note is turned upwards, so read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A musical note written out for use at a fee-paying school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English fee-paying school, which the British call a public school.

clue.text: Informed on direction to be taken in slump

indicators.note: the compass letter is to be taken into the middle of the word for a slump

parts.note: to sag is to slump or droop
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone told on a colleague about which way to go during an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a criminal who sang to the police informed on accomplices, like squealed.

clue.text: Getting irate in forced inactivity

indicators.note: the letters of irate in are forced into a new shape

explanation.surface: Becoming angry when made to sit idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is only a link; 'forced' rearranges IRATE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay still, a sluggish lack of activity.

clue.text: Radical accepting organisation is hard to understand

indicators.note: the word for radical accepts, i.e. takes inside it, the abbreviation for an organisation

parts.note: radical in the sense of fundamental, built in, is inherent
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business organisation

explanation.surface: A political extremist taking up with a group is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks like a person, but it means 'fundamental' here, INHERENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherent speech or writing is muddled and makes no sense, so it is hard to follow.

clue.text: Heartless rogue with a riddle he's holding back

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters of rogue, leaving just its first and last

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, a kind of strainer

explanation.surface: A villain without feeling who sets a puzzle while keeping something back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' suggests a puzzle, but it is the sieve sense, used for sifting soil or gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who curbs or keeps a thing in check is one who restrains it.

clue.text: Constituents never once get together again

indicators.note: the constituents, or component letters, of never once are reassembled

explanation.surface: Voters who have never met are told to gather once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' reads as voters, but it is the anagram signal: the parts of NEVER ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble again after a break, as a meeting or court does.

clue.text: Left one wanting companionship

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned and longing for company.
explanation.definitionFit: A lone person is solitary, lacking any companion.

clue.text: It takes money and a little science to copy a work of art

parts.note: L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra, so money
taken as written
Sc is the short form of science, as in BSc
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: Forging a famous painting needs cash and some technical knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes' and 'to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of rural scenery is a classic genre of artwork.

clue.text: Awfully pricey nag gaining high praise

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of pricey nag are in a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: An overpriced old horse being lavishly acclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a formal speech or text of lavish tribute.

clue.text: The Spanish military leader appears wooden

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: the leader of military is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish general looks stiff and expressionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wooden' reads as stiff, but it means made of a particular wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood tree, so a thing of elm is made of timber.

clue.text: No approved retreat

parts.note: taken as written
OK means approved or accepted

explanation.surface: Permission refused for a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small secluded corner, a quiet hideaway.

clue.text: In a strange mood — decidedly strange

indicators.note: in tells you the letters are sitting inside the run mood decidedly

explanation.surface: Feeling peculiar, really very peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and peculiar are synonyms for out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Conservative proposal about honour causing uproar

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, surrounding, the abbreviation for the honour

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A Tory motion about awards provoking a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an honour given by the British monarch; 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion is a noisy disturbance, a tumult.

clue.text: Make allegations against junior for nothing at all

parts.note: to charge someone is to accuse them
less can mean younger or minor, as in St James the Less

explanation.surface: Accusing a junior employee without grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less' meaning the younger is old-fashioned, surviving in names such as James the Less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no charge costs nothing, it is free.

clue.text: They grouse if there are many people passing forged notes!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a great many
to utter is to put counterfeit money into circulation, so these are utterers

explanation.surface: A gang of counterfeiters spreading fake banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' has a legal sense, to pass forged money. 'if there are' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: People who complain under their breath grumble, which is what grousers do.

clue.text: Foreigner finding new land-route

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of land-route are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A stranger discovering a fresh overland path.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlander is someone from abroad, an alien or stranger.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

explanation.surface: A loyal backer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to staunch it; a plant's stem holds up its leaves and flower.

clue.text: Tart and pie cooked and divided into sections

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of tart and pie are mixed up and altered

explanation.surface: A tart and a pie baked and then cut into portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Partite describes something split into parts, as in bipartite.

clue.text: Quite unperturbed when cut after about fifty

indicators.note: after places the word for cut later than the letters for about and fifty

parts.note: re means about or concerning
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
axed means cut or chopped

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm after being sacked at fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed means calm and at ease, free of worry.

clue.text: Disrupt a mountaineer's holiday?

explanation.surface: Spoiling a climber's vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a climber's holiday would be a break spent up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up a meeting is to disrupt it; a climber's holiday is a break spent up high.

clue.text: A monstrous creature, so should be retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for so is drawn back to front

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A beast so terrible it ought to be put out to pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are giant man-eating monsters of folklore.

clue.text: Bond's men finding themselves in a welcome situation

indicators.note: the word men find themselves placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to greet is to welcome someone

explanation.surface: James Bond's henchmen being warmly received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it means a pact; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding pact or contract, an accord.

clue.text: Duck occupying a scholar — a big old bird

indicators.note: the letter for duck occupies, sits inside, the scholar's degree

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a degree held by a scholar
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so O

explanation.surface: A duck hanging round a learned person, a large ancient bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nil score in cricket, the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a huge flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct.

clue.text: Manage to move quickly

explanation.surface: Someone coping by hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it; to run is to go fast on foot.

clue.text: Outlet for fuel distribution

indicators.note: distribution means the letters of fuel are spread around in a new order

explanation.surface: A channel through which fuel is shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a duct carrying smoke out of a chimney.

clue.text: A stern view of the ocean

definitions.text: A stern view of the ocean

parts.words: A stern view of the ocean
parts.note: read stern as the back of a ship: the eddying sea seen just behind the vessel as it moves

explanation.surface: A grim opinion of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' reads as severe, but it is the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use the term for the slack eddying sea close astern of a moving ship.

clue.text: Quarters accommodating five hundred couples

indicators.note: the compass letters accommodate, take inside them, the Roman numeral

parts.note: W, E and S are compass points, the quarters of the compass
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Lodgings housing five hundred pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, joining two people as a pair.

clue.text: Saving up — a musical instrument's wanted

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for saving is read from bottom to top

parts.note: saving in the sense of except is but

explanation.surface: Putting money aside because someone wants a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like putting money by, but it means 'except', BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the large low brass instrument of a band.

clue.text: Badly organised tour becomes a disorderly flight

indicators.note: badly organised tells you the letters of tour are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A poorly planned trip turns into a chaotic retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is the panicked retreat of a beaten army.

clue.text: As is written repeatedly, she was worshipped at one time

definitions.text: she was worshipped at one time

indicators.note: the word is is written out twice in a row

explanation.surface: A remark about a goddess, with 'as is' repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a goddess of ancient Egypt, revered in antiquity.

clue.text: A swinging alternative!

parts.note: playground rides: the thing offered instead of the swings, as in the saying about swings and gains and losses

explanation.surface: Something offered as a lively option.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'swings and roundabouts' means gains on one side balance losses on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairground and playground rides pair the swing with a rotating platform in the familiar saying.
